subject.title: fix(browser): keep tab reachability retry delay abortable

question: Does the route-level real-timer result plus the separate real-Chrome helper result sufficiently prove this three-line browser retry change, or must the contributor demonstrate an actual OpenClaw-managed tab mutation cancelled inside the retry window?
rationale: The implementation and supplemental evidence are strong, but the external-PR proof policy normally requires the changed behavior to run through a real setup; only a maintainer can authorize a proportional proof override.

options.title: Accept composite proof
options.body: Apply a proof override and continue normal merge review because the route harness, real Chrome timing, existing no-mutation regression test, and narrow helper substitution jointly establish the behavior.

options.title: Require managed-browser proof
options.body: Keep the proof gate until a redacted terminal transcript, logs, or recording shows close, focus, or select cancelled during the retry delay with prompt return and no later mutation.

recommendation.title: Accept composite proof
recommendation.body: Apply a proof override and continue normal merge review because the route harness, real Chrome timing, existing no-mutation regression test, and narrow helper substitution jointly establish the behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties this person most directly to ownership of the bundled browser implementation, and the decision concerns proportional evidence for that surface.
